title: The Syntax of Propositional Logic
subtopics: Propositional alphabet: variables, connectives, auxiliary symbols

definitions.definition: An atomic symbol from the set A = {p, q, r, p', q₁, …} that can be assigned a truth value.
A formula built inductively from propositional variables using connectives ¬, ∧, ∨ (and → ↔).
A tree representation of a formula where internal nodes are connectives and leaves are propositional variables.
A formula φ is a subformula of ψ if φ appears as a subtree in the AST of ψ.
The size of a formula is the number of nodes in its AST.

algorithms: AST construction from a formula string
formulas: PL ::= A | ⊥ | ¬PL | (PL ∧ PL) | (PL ∨ PL) | (PL → PL) | (PL ↔ PL)
examples: pq is not a valid formula
learning_objectives: Define the alphabet of propositional logic.
Construct and recognise syntactically valid propositional formulae.
Build and read abstract syntax trees.
Define and compute subformulae and formula size.
